title: On-call and Incident Response Playbook: incidents, runbooks, postmortems, rotations, game days, status & comms templates
author: Priya Nair
body:
Purpose

This playbook codifies Redwood Inference's standard on-call and incident response process. It provides:
- Severity definitions and SLO-linked thresholds
- Roles & responsibilities during an incident
- A step-by-step incident lifecycle (triage -> mitigation -> recovery -> review)
- Runbook and postmortem templates and examples
- On-call rotation and escalation policy
- Quarterly game day guidance and checklists
- Status page and customer communication templates

Scope

Applies to all production-facing services that impact customer inference (hosted API, dedicated endpoints, private deployments) including: api-gateway, inference-runtime, kv-cache, routing-service, auth-service, and console. For team-specific runbooks, link to the service page under eng-platform.

Quick links

- Incident channel: #incident-redwood (Slack)
- Pager duty: Redwood Oncall (Primary/Secondary)
- Status page: https://status.redwood-inference.internal
- Runbook index: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-index

1) Severity taxonomy and SLO mapping

- Sev 1 (Critical): Customer-facing outages or severe degradation (service unavailable or >50% traffic errors) impacting multiple customers or major revenue paths.
  - Target response: acknowledge within 5 minutes.
  - Target mitigation window: 1 hour to restore customer traffic to >90% baseline.
  - Typical examples: inference-runtime OOM crash cluster-wide, API gateway major region outage.

- Sev 2 (High): Significant degradation for a subset of customers or non-critical functionality (e.g., increased latency, partial feature failure).
  - Acknowledge within 15 minutes.
  - Mitigate within 4 hours or apply a documented workaround.
  - Example: p50/p95 latency regressions for a single model or region, KV cache 20% miss spike.

- Sev 3 (Medium): Minor impact or single-customer issues with an available workaround.
  - Acknowledge within 4 hours.
  - Resolve in next business day or via backlog ticket.

- Sev 4 (Low): Operational tasks, scheduled maintenance, or non-urgent requests.

SLO & alert examples (reference):
- inference-runtime: p99 latency < 750ms (SLO), alert if p99 > 1000ms for 5m
- api-gateway: 99.9% success rate (SLO), alert on 5xx rate > 1% for 5m or request error rate growth > 2x baseline
- kv-cache: cache hit rate >= 85%, alert if hit rate < 70% for 10m

2) Roles & responsibilities

- First Responder (Primary on-call): Own initial triage, run initial runbook steps, escalate as required.
- Secondary on-call: Provide backup and take over if Primary is unavailable or incident expands.
- Incident Commander (IC): Coordinates cross-team activity for Sev1/Sev2 incidents, maintains incident timeline, and owns status communications. Usually an SRE manager or senior engineer.
- Communications Lead: Drafts public and internal status updates; liaises with customer success for external messaging.
- Mitigation Engineers: Engineers from product teams (runtime, gateway, infra) who execute service-specific remediation.
- Postmortem Owner: Owns RCA and action item follow-through post-incident (typically the service owner).

3) Incident lifecycle (step-by-step)

1. Detection & Alerting
   - Alerts are routed to PagerDuty. On-call escalations follow the PD schedule (Primary -> Secondary -> IC).
   - On Slack: create an incident channel #incident-<yyyymmdd>-<short-name> and pin the incident template (see templates below).

2. Triage (First 0-15 minutes)
   - Primary acknowledges the Pd alert and posts to #incident with: severity, affected services, first-observed timestamp, and immediate mitigations attempted.
   - Run quick impact assessment: which regions/customers, traffic percentages, any ongoing deployments?
   - If Sev1/Sev2, IC is notified within 15 minutes.

3. Containment & Mitigation (15-60 minutes)
   - Follow the service runbook for mitigation. Common mitigations: scale up replicas, roll back latest deployment, redirect traffic via routing policy, disable degraded feature flags.
   - Track every action in the incident timeline (Slack timeline or shared doc).

4. Recovery (within mitigation window)
   - Verify traffic and error metrics have returned to acceptable levels per SLO.
   - If partial recovery, apply short-term mitigations and define customer-facing messaging.

5. Communication
   - Internal: IC posts hourly updates for Sev1 until the incident is resolved; less frequent for lower severities.
   - External: Communications Lead posts a status page update for Sev1/Sev2 incidents within 30-60 minutes after triage. See templates below.

6. Post-Incident Review
   - Create a postmortem within 3 business days (owner assigned at incident close).
   - Postmortem must be published to Confluence and a 30-45 minute review meeting scheduled within 7 business days for Sev1 incidents.

4) Runbook template (copy into service-specific runbooks)

- Runbook header: service name, owner, contact PD rotation, link to dashboards, repository and deployment pipelines.
- Preconditions: symptoms that trigger this runbook (alerts/metrics).
- Quick checks (commands & dashboards):
  1. Check pods & nodes: kubectl --context prod get pods -l app=<service> -n prod
  2. Check logs for recent errors: kubectl logs --context prod -l app=<service> --since=15m
  3. Check Sentry/Datadog traces: link to dashboard
  4. Check recent deploys: deploy pipeline run history (CI link)
- Common mitigations (ordered):
  1. Scale service: kubectl scale deploy/<service> --replicas=<n>
  2. Roll back to last known good: ci rollback <service> --to=<commit>
  3. Evict pods on problem nodes: kubectl cordon/evict
  4. Purge cache keys: redis-cli -h <host> DEL <key-pattern>
- Safety checks & gating: ensure opt-out feature flags are available before toggling.
- Post-action verification: specific metrics to validate (error rate, latency, concurrency).

Example runbook excerpt for inference-runtime:
- Preconditions: p99 latency > 1000ms for 5m OR 5xx rate > 2% for 5m
- Quick checks:
  - datadog metric: inference-runtime.p99
  - kubectl get pods -l app=inference-runtime -n inference-prod
  - check GPU utilization: nvidia-smi on affected hosts via telemetry page
- Immediate mitigations:
  1. Temporarily scale up worker pool: kubectl scale deploy/inference-runtime --replicas=24
  2. If OOM patterns visible, enable model-eviction policy: curl -XPOST https://ops-api/models/evict?policy=least-recently-used
  3. If a new model binary was deployed in the last 30m, rollback via CI.

5) Postmortem template (required fields)

- Title: Incident YYYY-MM-DD — short description
- Severity: Sev1/Sev2/Sev3
- Owner: name and team
- Timeline: bullet timeline with UTC timestamps
- Impact summary: customers affected, duration, business impact, estimated lost requests/minutes
- Root cause: concise technical root cause statement
- Contributing factors: list of contributing issues (alerts, incorrect runbook step, automation gap)
- Resolution & mitigations: what was done to resolve and stop-gap measures
- Long-term fixes / action items: owner, ETA, verification plan
- Detection & tooling gaps: what alerts, dashboards or logs are missing or noisy
- Lessons learned: process and communication improvements
- Links: runbooks, dashboards, PRs, deploy history

Action item example format:
- [P0] Fix model eviction race condition — owner: @mfernandez — ETA: 2026-03-15 — verification: simulated scale test in staging

6) On-call rotations & escalation

- Primary on-call: weekly rotation (Mon 09:00 UTC -> Mon 09:00 UTC).
- Secondary on-call: weekly, offset by 1 week.
- Escalation timeline:
  - 0 min: PagerDuty to Primary (ack required within 5/15/240 minutes depending on severity).
  - 15 min: notify Secondary if no ack for Sev1.
  - 30 min: notify IC and Engineering Manager for Sev1.
  - 60 min: escalate to Director of SRE / CTL for unresolved Sev1.
- On-call expectations:
  - Primary must be reachable during on-call hours and carry an on-call device with PD notifications enabled.
  - If on-call Primary needs to transfer, they must hand off in the rotation doc and update PD schedules.

7) Game days (quarterly)

Purpose: Validate runbooks, alerting, and cross-team coordination.

Frequency & owners:
- Quarterly game day organized by Eng SRE (calendar owned by eng-sre@redwood-inference.internal).
- Product/service teams required to participate annually.

Game day format:
1. Prepare (2 weeks prior): pick target service, create test plan, verify staging mirrors prod metrics.
2. Inject (day-of): execute controlled incident (e.g., simulate model memory leak, scale down replicas, increase error rate).
3. Run response: follow normal incident procedures, time to mitigate, whether runbooks are followed.
4. Review (post-mortem): publish findings and create action items.

Success criteria:
- Runbook steps were executed and completed without blocking.
- Alerts fired and were actionable.
- Communication templates were used and useful.

8) Status page & customer communication templates

Internal Slack incident starter (paste into new #incident-... channel):
"""
INCIDENT: <short-title>
Severity: <Sev1/Sev2/Sev3>
Service(s): <service-list>
First observed: <UTC timestamp>
Impact: <brief description>
Primary: @<primary> Secondary: @<secondary> IC: @<ic>
Immediate action: <what's being done>
Status page: <link once posted>
Incident channel: #incident-<yyyymmdd>-<short-name>
Timeline:
- <UTC time> — Alert received
"""

External status page template (short & factual):
Title: Degraded performance for <service> in <region>
Status: Investigating / Identified / Monitoring / Resolved
Detected: <UTC time>
Update cadence: Every 30-60 minutes for active Sev1/Sev2
Impact: Customers may experience increased latency or errors when calling inference endpoints in <region>.
Mitigation steps taken: Rolling back recent deploy / Scaling up runtime / Redirecting traffic to alternate region.
Next update: <UTC time>

Customer email template (for incidents affecting >10% of customers or high-revenue customers):
Subject: Incident affecting <service> (short summary)
Hi <Customer name>,
We detected an issue impacting <service> in <region> beginning <UTC time>. Our on-call team is actively investigating and has implemented mitigation steps to reduce impact. We will provide an update no later than <time>.
If you have urgent concerns, please contact your Customer Success lead or reply to this email and we will escalate.
Regards,
Redwood Inference Operations

9) Metrics, dashboards and alert hygiene

- Every alert must include: owner, severity, runbook link, runbook steps to verify.
- Alert rules should avoid noisy thresholds; prefer relative baselines (e.g., 2x baseline) and rolling-window checks.
- Dashboards: service overview (traffic, errors, latency p50/p95/p99, backend errors), infra overview (CPU/GPU utilization, memory, disk), dependency map.

Recommended alert examples (Datadog/Prometheus style):
- api-gateway: alert if 5xx rate > 1% for 5m AND request rate > 100 req/s
- inference-runtime: alert if p99 latency > 1000ms for 5m OR GPU memory usage > 90% for 10m
- kv-cache: hit rate < 70% for 10m

10) After-incident actions and SLAs for postmortem publication

- Postmortem draft: due within 3 business days.
- Postmortem review meeting: scheduled within 7 business days for Sev1 incidents and optional for Sev2/Sev3.
- Action item tracking: create tickets with P0/P1/P2 priorities in Jira; owners must update progress weekly until resolution.

Appendix A — Contact matrix (example)
- SRE on-call primary: @oncall-primary (pagerduty)
- SRE on-call secondary: @oncall-secondary
- Runtime team lead: @mfernandez
- Platform infra: @ethan.zhao

Appendix B — Example playbook checklist (for first responder)
- [ ] Acknowledge PagerDuty alert
- [ ] Create incident channel and post incident starter
- [ ] Run quick checks (pods, logs, dashboards)
- [ ] Notify IC if Sev1/Sev2
- [ ] Apply mitigation per runbook
- [ ] Post status page update if appropriate
- [ ] Track timeline and actions
- [ ] Close incident and create postmortem ticket

Appendix C — Example retention & log access notes
- Logs: production logs retained 30 days in Datadog; critical traces 90 days.
- Audit trails for Private deployments: customer-managed logs retained per contract.

Governance & continuous improvement

- Runbook review cadence: each service runbook must be reviewed quarterly by service owner and SRE.
- Game days and runbook drills: quarterly.
- Postmortem action closure: tracked to completion; overdue action escalation to eng manager after 30 days.

Contact & feedback

If you have questions or suggested improvements to this playbook, contact eng-sre@redwood-inference.internal or open a PR to the Confluence page.
